sections.title: Why the disconnect state must be tracked
prose: The new field `reported_as_connected` ensures a 'disconnected' notification is sent exactly once when the websocket is closed or callbacks are disarmed.
Without it, the charge point would not know if the last state sent was 'connected', leaving consumers unaware of the disconnection.

question.ask: Is the rationale for tracking the disconnect state now clearer?
question.answer: The section now explains why the field exists, not just what it does.

sections.title: When the charge point must send a disconnect
prose: `disarm_connection_callbacks()` returns `true` if the last state sent was 'connected' and no notification was dispatched yet.
This signals the charge point to send a 'disconnected' notification, as the websocket thread will not.

question.ask: Does the section now focus on the caller's responsibility?
question.answer: The prose clarifies when the charge point must act, not just the mechanics of the return value.

sections.title: Add a minimal disconnected-notification helper
prose: The new method `notify_connection_state_changed_disconnected()` sends only the 'disconnected' state to consumers, without the rest of the websocket teardown (timers, message queue).
It is used in `stop()` when `disarm_connection_callbacks()` reports that a notification is still needed.

sections.title: Dispatch the notification in stop
prose: In `stop()`, after `disarm_connection_callbacks()` returns `true`, the charge point calls `notify_connection_state_changed_disconnected()` to send the final 'disconnected' state to consumers.
This ensures that consumers always see the transition, even when the websocket thread is torn down first.

sections.title: Update the mock for tests
prose: The mock in the test suite is updated to match the new return type of `disarm_connection_callbacks()`.

sections.title: Also changed in lib/everest/ocpp (2 files)
prose: 2 files, 2 changed lines the story above does not show.

overview: This change ensures that OCPP charge points report a 'disconnected' state to consumers when they are stopped, even if the websocket thread is torn down first.
The core problem is that `disarm_connection_callbacks()` used to suppress all connection-state notifications, including the final 'disconnected' one that consumers expect when the charge point stops.
The fix adds a state-tracking field in `ConnectivityManager` and makes `disarm_connection_callbacks()` return whether a notification is still needed. Callers then dispatch it manually.
